rules.statement: Under the Kandyan law prior to 1939, a daughter who went out in Diga forfeited her rights to her paternal estate even if there was no valid registered marriage between her and the man or men with whom she had Diga connections.
rules.supporting_quote: "In Kalu v. Howwa Kiri [(1892) 2 Ceylon Law Reports 54.] it was held that the exclusion of a Diga married daughter from a share of her father's property attaches to a daughter who goes out in Diga, even though the marriage is invalid by reason of its non-registration under the provisions of Ordinance 3 of 1870."
